get.description:
Decision support only -- see schemas.COMPETENCY_PROFILE_DISCLAIMER.
Purely additive aggregation of whatever's been scored so far; never
auto-certifies, never calls itself a pass/fail.

Dual auth, same as GET /assessments/{id} -- assessor/admin JWT, or
this assessment's own (active) worker token.

Photos serve their own bytes directly (no separate thumbnail job --
see models.EvidenceItem.thumbnail_status's 'not_applicable' default).
Videos serve the ffmpeg-extracted frame once the background job
completes; while queued, or if ffmpeg extraction failed/is unavailable,
this is a graceful 404 (never a 500) so the dashboard can show a
pending/placeholder state instead of crashing.

Protected -- same dual auth as GET /assessments/{id} (assessor/admin
JWT, or this assessment's own worker token).

post.description:
An assessor picks a submitted assessment off the queue -- moves
submitted -> in_review and claims it (assessor_id).

The worker app calls this once it's done capturing evidence for all
five tasks -- moves draft -> submitted and LOCKS further evidence
uploads (see routers/uploads.py's require_draft checks). Worker-token
authenticated, same as uploads -- there is no worker login.

No new token is issued -- every worker-token-authenticated endpoint
(uploads, submit, GET, report download) rejects it from this point on,
regardless of whether the hash would otherwise still match.

Invalidates the current token immediately (the old raw value stops
working the instant this commits -- its hash is simply overwritten) and
issues a fresh one, returned once, exactly like at creation. Use when a
worker's device is lost or a token may have leaked.

get.description:
Submitted (or further-along) assessments waiting on an assessor,
oldest first. Assessor/admin only -- see server/app/auth.py. No scoring
here yet -- that's P6/P7.

Public, unauthenticated -- the whole point of signing is that anyone
can check a report's authenticity without needing credentials. Returns
only a valid/invalid verdict and signing metadata; never the report
content, scores, or any evidence.
